Questions, answered

Do I need to know how to code?

No. Describe what should happen in game, such as the trigger, the effect and how long it lasts, and ModHorizon writes the project. The Java stays readable if you want to learn from it or edit it by hand.

Which loaders and versions are supported?

Paper, Folia, Purpur, Spigot, Bukkit and Sponge plugins; Velocity and BungeeCord proxy plugins; and Fabric, Quilt, Forge and NeoForge mods. Every stable Minecraft release each loader shipped is available, from 1.1 up to 26.3.

What happens if I pick a version a loader doesn't support?

ModHorizon tells you straight away that the pair can't be used, with a Why? button that explains the reason, such as Fabric starting at 1.14 or NeoForge splitting from Forge at 1.20.1. It also suggests the closest version or a loader that does work.

Do I get a .jar I can install?

When a build service is connected, sources are compiled in an isolated worker with the right Java version for your target, and the .jar is ready to download. Without one you still get the full source preview, but no compiled file.

What happens when a build fails?

Compiler errors go back to the model for up to three repair attempts. Every revision is validated again before the next build, and the full log stays visible.

Is generated code safe to run?

Treat it like any third-party plugin or mod: it runs with full access to your server or game. ModHorizon only accepts Java sources and recognised descriptors, rejects build scripts and unexpected paths, and you can read every line before installing.
